tests.title: --detail is registered on Common, defaulting to summary and accepting full
given: a Common flag set is registered for a tool
tests.when: the tool is invoked with no --detail flag, and separately with --detail full
then: the first run's Common.Detail is "summary"
the second run's Common.Detail is "full"
tests.pseudocode: c := &Common{}; fs := flag.NewFlagSet(); c.Register(fs); fs.Parse([]); assert c.Detail == "summary"; fs2.Parse(["--detail","full"]); assert c.Detail == "full"

tests.title: An unrecognized --detail value is a usage error before any input is resolved
given: a tool invocation with --detail wrong and a plain-text positional argument
then: the process exits with code 2
the envelope's error.category is "usage"
no file is read, no issue is fetched, and no model is resolved
tests.pseudocode: res := runCLI(tool, "--detail", "wrong", "some text"); assert res.ExitCode == 2; assert res.Envelope.Error.Category == "usage"

tests.title: The --detail full view's keys are always a superset of what full carried before this spec, for every tool
given: a successful run recorded for each of issue, fix, spec and impl
tests.when: for any of the four tools, the --detail full result's JSON keys are compared against the pre-06 full result's JSON keys for an equivalent run
then: every pre-06 key is present in the post-06 full view
no pre-06 key is missing or restructured
tests.pseudocode: for tool in [issue, fix, spec, impl]: pre := preSpecFullKeys(tool); post := runFull(tool).ResultKeys(); assert pre.isSubsetOf(post)

tests.title: Every tool's Result records which detail view was emitted, under both summary and full
given: a completed run of each of issue, fix, spec and impl
tests.when: the envelope is built under --detail summary and again under --detail full
then: result.detail is "summary" for the summary run
result.detail is "full" for the full run
detail is present on all four tools' results in both cases
tests.pseudocode: for tool in [issue, fix, spec, impl]: assert runSummary(tool).Result["detail"] == "summary"; assert runFull(tool).Result["detail"] == "full"

tests.title: Every run writes the full-view envelope to a report file, regardless of --detail
given: a successful fix run under --detail summary
then: a report file exists on disk
the report file's result carries every field the full view carries, not the trimmed subset
tests.pseudocode: r := runCLI("fix", "--detail", "summary", input); rf := readFile(r.Envelope.ReportFile); assert rf.Result.HasField("implementation")

tests.title: The default report-file path is computed under XDG_STATE_HOME with a colon-free timestamp and its parent directory is created
given: XDG_STATE_HOME set to a temp directory
no --report-file given
then: the report file exists at $XDG_STATE_HOME/agent-fox/runs/issue-<timestamp>-<pid>.json
the timestamp segment contains no colon
the parent directory was created by the run
tests.pseudocode: os.Setenv("XDG_STATE_HOME", tmp); r := runCLI("issue", input); assert fileExists(filepath.Join(tmp, "agent-fox/runs", basename(r.Envelope.ReportFile)))

tests.title: The report-file path falls back to ~/.local/state when XDG_STATE_HOME is unset
given: XDG_STATE_HOME unset
HOME pointed at a temp directory
no --report-file given
then: the report file exists under <HOME>/.local/state/agent-fox/runs/
tests.pseudocode: os.Unsetenv("XDG_STATE_HOME"); os.Setenv("HOME", tmp); r := runCLI("spec", input); assert fileExists(filepath.Join(tmp, ".local/state/agent-fox/runs", basename(r.Envelope.ReportFile)))

tests.title: A report file that cannot be written records a low warning and omits report_file, without failing the run
given: a report-file directory that is read-only
tests.when: fix is run successfully to completion
then: the run's exit code and ok are unaffected by the write failure
warnings includes one entry with code report_file_not_written, severity low, stage report
the envelope has no report_file field
tests.pseudocode: makeReadOnly(reportDir); r := runCLI("fix", "--report-file", filepath.Join(reportDir, "x.json"), input); assert r.ExitCode == 0; assert r.Envelope.Warnings.Contains(code:"report_file_not_written"); assert !r.Envelope.HasField("report_file")

tests.title: A --dry-run run still writes its report file
given: a fix run invoked with --dry-run
then: a report file exists on disk at the computed or given path
tests.pseudocode: r := runCLI("fix", "--dry-run", input); assert fileExists(r.Envelope.ReportFile)

tests.title: report_file names the path actually written when the write succeeds
given: a writable report-file location
then: the envelope's top-level report_file equals the path the report was written to
the named file exists
tests.pseudocode: r := runCLI("impl", input); assert fileExists(r.Envelope.ReportFile); assert r.Envelope.ReportFile == expectedPath

tests.title: A report file is written for a failed run and for a post-classification usage error
given: an input that causes fix to fail its run
a separate invocation that fails a post-classification check
then: both emit a JSON object on stdout
both have a report file written naming the same content that was printed
tests.pseudocode: rFail := runCLI("fix", failingInput); assert fileExists(rFail.Envelope.ReportFile); rUsage := runCLI("fix", "--input-kind", "issue", "not a url"); assert fileExists(rUsage.Envelope.ReportFile)

tests.title: A bare invocation, -h/--help and --version print no JSON and write no report file
given: a terminal-attached bare invocation
an invocation with -h
an invocation with --version
then: no JSON object appears on stdout beyond the existing terminal/help/version text
no file appears at any report-file location
tests.pseudocode: for args in [[], ["-h"], ["--version"]]: r := runCLI("issue", args...); assert !looksLikeJSON(r.Stdout); assert countFiles(reportsDir) == before

tests.title: The report file's content is byte-for-byte identical to what --detail full would have printed for the same run
given: identical, deterministic inputs for two runs of issue: one --detail summary, one --detail full
then: the summary run's report file bytes equal the full run's stdout bytes
tests.pseudocode: rs := runCLI("issue", "--detail", "summary", input); rf := runCLI("issue", "--detail", "full", input); assert readFile(rs.Envelope.ReportFile) == rf.Stdout

tests.title: issue's summary view keeps exactly the documented subset, with affected_files reduced to paths only
given: an issuetriage.Result with action, repo, url, number, title, severity, confidence, affected_files, labels, rejected_path_calls and other fields set
then: result carries exactly action, repo, url, number, title, severity, confidence, affected_files, labels, rejected_path_calls plus detail
each affected_files entry is a bare path string, not an object with role
tests.pseudocode: s := res.SummaryView(); assert keys(s) == {action,repo,url,number,title,severity,confidence,affected_files,labels,rejected_path_calls,detail}; assert isStringArray(s.affected_files)

tests.title: fix's summary view omits verification when the run's verdict is landable
given: a codefix.Result whose Verification.Verdict.Landable() reports true
then: result has no verification field
result still carries stage, branch, base_branch, commit, changed_files, verdict, criteria_outcome, pull_request_url, dry_run
tests.pseudocode: s := res.SummaryView(); assert !s.HasField("verification"); assert s.HasFields(stage,branch,base_branch,commit,changed_files,verdict,criteria_outcome,pull_request_url,dry_run)

tests.title: fix's summary view includes verification, tail output and all, when the run's verdict is not landable
given: a codefix.Result whose Verification.Verdict.Landable() reports false
then: result carries a verification field
that field includes the failing command's tail output
tests.pseudocode: s := res.SummaryView(); assert s.HasField("verification"); assert len(s.verification.TailOutput) > 0

tests.title: impl's summary view reduces each task to {id, outcome, commit, verdict} and omits top-level verification when the stopping verdict is landable
given: a codeimpl.Result with several TaskReport entries and a landable top-level verdict
then: each task entry in result.tasks carries only id, outcome, commit, verdict
result has no top-level verification field
the task counts and package fields are present
tests.pseudocode: s := res.SummaryView(); for t in s.tasks: assert keys(t) == {id,outcome,commit,verdict}; assert !s.HasField("verification")

tests.title: impl's summary view includes the top-level verification when the stopping verdict is not landable
given: a codeimpl.Result whose stopping verdict fails codeimpl/gate.go's landable() check
then: result carries a top-level verification field with the gate's checks and tail output
tests.pseudocode: s := res.SummaryView(); assert s.HasField("verification"); assert len(s.verification.Checks) > 0

tests.title: spec's summary view reduces validation and traceability and drops follow_on_specs and split_plan
given: a specgen.Result with a full Validation, a full Traceability, follow_on_specs and split_plan populated
then: result.validation carries only valid, error_count, errors
result.traceability carries only criteria_uncovered, paths_uncovered, tests_unowned
result has no follow_on_specs and no split_plan field
result still carries spec_dir, spec_id, spec_name, status, artifacts, open_questions, split
tests.pseudocode: s := res.SummaryView(); assert keys(s.validation) == {valid,error_count,errors}; assert keys(s.traceability) == {criteria_uncovered,paths_uncovered,tests_unowned}; assert !s.HasField("follow_on_specs"); assert !s.HasField("split_plan")

tests.title: Fields trimmed from the summary view are still computed in full and are present, unabridged, in the report file
given: a fix run under --detail summary whose verdict is landable, so verification is trimmed from stdout
then: stdout's result has no verification field
the report file's result carries a fully computed verification field, identical to what a --detail full run would compute
tests.pseudocode: r := runCLI("fix", "--detail", "summary", input); assert !r.Envelope.Result.HasField("verification"); rf := readFile(r.Envelope.ReportFile); full := runCLI("fix", "--detail", "full", input); assert rf.Result.verification == full.Envelope.Result.verification

tests.title: artifacts entries carry exactly the fields fixed for their kind
given: a fix run that created a branch, one commit, and opened a pull request
then: artifacts contains a branch entry with exactly {kind,name,base}
a commit entry with exactly {kind,sha,branch}
a pull_request entry with exactly {kind,url,number}
tests.pseudocode: a := res.Artifacts(); branch := a.find(kind=="branch"); assert keys(branch) == {kind,name,base}; pr := a.find(kind=="pull_request"); assert keys(pr) == {kind,url,number}

tests.title: artifacts is built only from the Result's already-established fact fields, never from the model's own report
given: a codefix.Result whose Implementation text is mutated after the pipeline ran, while Branch, Commit and PullRequestURL are unchanged
tests.when: artifacts is recomputed for that Result
then: the artifacts array is identical to what it was before Implementation was mutated
tests.pseudocode: before := res.Artifacts(); res.Implementation = "anything else entirely"; after := res.Artifacts(); assert before == after

tests.title: Under --dry-run, a hypothetical pull_request, comment or issue entry is marked dry_run: true
given: a fix run with --dry-run --land=pr, so no pull request was actually opened
an issue run with --dry-run, so no issue was actually filed
then: the fix run's pull_request artifact entry carries dry_run: true
the issue run's issue artifact entry carries dry_run: true with an empty url and number
tests.pseudocode: prEntry := fixRes.Artifacts().find(kind=="pull_request"); assert prEntry.dry_run == true; issueEntry := issueRes.Artifacts().find(kind=="issue"); assert issueEntry.dry_run == true && issueEntry.url == "" && issueEntry.number == 0

tests.title: Under --dry-run, the branch and commit entries carry no dry_run marker
given: a fix run with --dry-run that still creates a branch and a commit locally
then: the branch entry has no dry_run field
the commit entry has no dry_run field
tests.pseudocode: a := res.Artifacts(); branch := a.find(kind=="branch"); commit := a.find(kind=="commit"); assert !branch.HasField("dry_run"); assert !commit.HasField("dry_run")

tests.title: The existing result fields are unchanged alongside the new artifacts array
given: a fix run that produced a pull request
then: result.pull_request_url still carries the URL directly, unchanged
artifacts additionally carries the same URL under its pull_request entry
tests.pseudocode: r := runCLI("fix", input); assert r.Envelope.Result.pull_request_url == r.Envelope.Artifacts.find(kind=="pull_request").url

tests.title: side_effects lists every remote write in order and is omitted when there were none
given: an issue run that creates an issue and posts no comment
a spec run that never wrote to a forge
then: the issue run's side_effects has one entry with action create_issue, ok, target and optional warning fields present
the spec run's envelope has no side_effects field at all
tests.pseudocode: assert issueEnv.SideEffects[0].action == "create_issue"; assert !specEnv.HasField("side_effects")

tests.title: side_effects actions are drawn from the closed set and each target is named by its documented convention
given: a fix run that pushes a branch, opens a PR, and posts a comment; an issue run that updates an existing issue
then: every action is one of create_issue, update_issue, comment, push, open_pr
the push entry's target is "origin <branch>"
the comment entry's target is "<owner>/<repo>#<number>"
the open_pr entry's target is "<owner>/<repo>#<pr-number>"
tests.pseudocode: for e in res.SideEffects(): assert e.action in {create_issue,update_issue,comment,push,open_pr}; push := find(action==push); assert push.target == fmt("origin %s", branch); openPr := find(action==open_pr); assert openPr.target == fmt("%s/%s#%d", owner, repo, prNumber)

tests.title: A failed write is recorded with ok: false and the same WarnCode the call site already recorded
given: a fix run whose push to origin fails, and the pipeline records a Run.Warn for that failure
then: the push entry has ok: false
the push entry's warning equals the WarnCode the pipeline's Run.Warn call recorded for that failure
no side_effects entry has ok: true for that same failed push
tests.pseudocode: e := res.SideEffects().find(action=="push"); assert e.ok == false; assert e.warning == run.Warnings.find(stage=="push").Code

tests.title: Each side_effects entry is recorded live at its actual write call site, in the order writes happened
given: an issuetriage run whose Write path both creates an issue and posts a follow-up comment via a fake forge client
then: side_effects has a create_issue entry followed by a comment entry, in that order
the order matches the order the fake forge client received the two calls
tests.pseudocode: fake := newFakeForge(); r := runIssuetriage(fake, input); assert r.SideEffects[0].action == "create_issue"; assert r.SideEffects[1].action == "comment"; assert fake.CallOrder == ["CreateIssue","PostComment"]

tests.title: side_effects is empty under --dry-run even for a run that would otherwise push, comment or open a PR
given: a fix run with --dry-run --land=pr on a change that would normally push and open a pull request
then: the envelope has no side_effects field, or an empty side_effects array
tests.pseudocode: r := runCLI("fix", "--dry-run", "--land", "pr", input); assert isEmptyOrAbsent(r.Envelope.SideEffects)

tests.title: issue suggests fix on the filed issue's URL, naming labels, when not run under --dry-run
given: an issuetriage.Result with Action "created", a URL, and labels ["bug","triaged"]
then: next has one entry with tool fix, input the issue URL, empty flags, and why mentioning the labels
tests.pseudocode: n := res.Next(); assert len(n) == 1; assert n[0].tool == "fix"; assert n[0].input == res.URL; assert contains(n[0].why, "bug") && contains(n[0].why, "triaged")

tests.title: spec suggests impl on the first written package that validates
given: a specgen.Result with two written packages, the second of which validates and the first does not
then: next contains an entry naming tool impl, input the second (validating) package's spec_dir, and the fixed why sentence
tests.pseudocode: n := res.Next(); e := n.find(tool=="impl"); assert e.input == validatingPkg.SpecDir

tests.title: spec suggests spec again on the literal origin when the split is unfinished and the input had a file or issue origin
given: a specgen.Result whose SplitPlan is non-empty and whose input origin was a file path
then: next contains a second entry naming tool spec, input the literal file path
tests.pseudocode: n := res.Next(); e := n.filter(tool=="spec")[0]; assert e.input == originalFilePath

tests.title: spec's resume suggestion uses the needs_human.resume placeholder when the input was raw text or stdin
given: a specgen.Result whose SplitPlan is non-empty and whose input was raw text with no stable origin
then: the spec-resume entry's input is exactly "<same input>"
tests.pseudocode: n := res.Next(); e := n.filter(tool=="spec")[0]; assert e.input == "<same input>"

tests.title: impl suggests itself on the same spec directory when the run parked
given: a codeimpl.Result with stage "parked"
then: next contains an entry naming tool impl, input the spec_dir, and why mentioning that re-running continues from the last landed task
tests.pseudocode: n := res.Next(); e := n[0]; assert e.tool == "impl"; assert e.input == res.SpecDir; assert contains(e.why, "continues from the last landed task")

tests.title: impl's parked-with-red-baseline suggestion adds --repair when no repair was attempted
given: a codeimpl.Result with stage "parked", a baseline whose checks include a failing one, and no Repair field set
then: the impl next entry's flags include "--repair"
the why text states the baseline needs repairing first
tests.pseudocode: e := res.Next()[0]; assert contains(e.flags, "--repair"); assert contains(e.why, "repair")

tests.title: fix's ambiguity next entry is character-for-character identical to needs_human.resume
given: a codefix.Result whose error category is "ambiguous"
tests.when: next and needs_human are both built for the same Result
then: next contains exactly one entry suggesting fix --context
that entry's input string is character-for-character identical to needs_human.resume
tests.pseudocode: n := res.Next(); nh := res.NeedsHuman(); e := n[0]; assert contains(e.flags, "--context"); assert e.input == nh.Resume

tests.title: fix produces no next entry on a run that lands successfully
given: a codefix.Result whose stage is a successful landing
then: next is absent or empty
tests.pseudocode: n := res.Next(); assert isEmptyOrAbsent(n)

tests.title: next entries are derived purely from Result fields, omitted when there is nothing to suggest, and are runnable exactly as printed
given: a specgen.Result with no validating package and no unfinished split
an issuetriage.Result with Action "none"
tests.when: next is built for each, and the underlying model-authored report text is mutated without changing any fact field
then: both envelopes omit next entirely
for a Result that does produce next entries, mutating the model-authored report text does not change the produced entries
tests.pseudocode: assert !specRes.Next(); assert !issueRes.Next(); before := fixRes.Next(); fixRes.Implementation = "different text"; assert fixRes.Next() == before

tests.title: A single-line, whitespace-free, path-shaped argument that does not exist is flagged with a high-severity warning naming it
given: the argument "widget/report.txt", which does not exist on disk
then: the classification is text
a warning with code input_looks_like_path, severity high, stage input is recorded
the warning's message names "widget/report.txt"
tests.pseudocode: in, warns := ResolveWithWarnings(ctx, "widget/report.txt", nil, nil); assert in.Kind == KindText; w := warns.find(code=="input_looks_like_path"); assert w.Severity == "high"; assert contains(w.Message, "widget/report.txt")

tests.title: An existing directory argument does not trigger the mistyped-path warning
given: an existing directory path, e.g. "src"
then: no input_looks_like_path warning is recorded for that argument
tests.pseudocode: in, warns := ResolveWithWarnings(ctx, "src", nil, nil); assert !warns.any(code=="input_looks_like_path")

tests.title: The mistyped-path warning is always in top-level warnings regardless of --detail, and appends the deterministic summary clause on an ok run
given: a run that succeeds (ok: true) with an input_looks_like_path warning recorded
tests.when: the envelope is built under --detail summary and again under --detail full
then: both envelopes' top-level warnings array includes the input_looks_like_path entry
summary carries the appended high-severity clause
tests.pseudocode: rs := runCLI(tool, "--detail", "summary", pathLikeInput); rf := runCLI(tool, "--detail", "full", pathLikeInput); assert rs.Envelope.Warnings.any(code=="input_looks_like_path"); assert rf.Envelope.Warnings.any(code=="input_looks_like_path"); assert contains(rs.Envelope.Summary, clauseFor("input_looks_like_path"))

tests.title: The presence of an input_looks_like_path warning does not affect what fix's or impl's summary view keeps for verification/baseline
given: a fix run and an impl run, each with a landable verdict and an input_looks_like_path warning recorded
tests.when: the summary view is built for each
then: fix's summary still omits verification, exactly as it would without the warning
impl's summary still omits verification, exactly as it would without the warning
tests.pseudocode: withWarning := buildSummary(landableFixResWithWarning); without := buildSummary(landableFixResNoWarning); assert withWarning.HasField("verification") == without.HasField("verification")

tests.title: --input-kind is registered on Common accepting only file, text, issue or stdin
given: a Common flag set is registered
tests.when: --input-kind is given each of the four legal values, and then an illegal value
then: each legal value is accepted
the illegal value is a usage error
tests.pseudocode: for k in ["file","text","issue","stdin"]: assert parseOK("--input-kind", k); assert parseFails("--input-kind", "bogus")

tests.title: --input-kind file refuses a missing path, naming that it does not exist
given: --input-kind file and a path that does not exist
then: the run exits with code 2
the error names that the path does not exist
tests.pseudocode: r := runCLI("fix", "--input-kind", "file", "/no/such/path.txt"); assert r.ExitCode == 2; assert contains(r.Stderr, "does not exist")

tests.title: --input-kind file refuses a directory, naming that it is one
given: --input-kind file and an existing directory path
then: the run exits with code 2
the error names that the path is a directory
tests.pseudocode: r := runCLI("fix", "--input-kind", "file", "src"); assert r.ExitCode == 2; assert contains(r.Stderr, "directory")

tests.title: --input-kind text uses the argument verbatim, ignoring a same-named file or a parseable URL
given: a file named "report.txt" existing on disk with different content than the argument string
an argument equal to "report.txt"
then: the resolved input's Body is the literal argument string "report.txt", not the file's contents
no file-existence or URL check occurred
tests.pseudocode: in := ResolveForced(ctx, "text", "report.txt", nil, nil); assert in.Body == "report.txt"; assert in.Kind == KindText

tests.title: --input-kind issue refuses an argument that does not parse as an issue URL, before any HTTP request
given: --input-kind issue and the argument "not a url"
then: the run exits with code 2
no HTTP request is made to any forge
tests.pseudocode: r := runCLIWithForgeSpy("issue", "--input-kind", "issue", "not a url"); assert r.ExitCode == 2; assert forgeSpy.RequestCount == 0

tests.title: --input-kind stdin refuses any argument other than "-"
given: --input-kind stdin and the argument "file.txt"
then: the run exits with code 2
tests.pseudocode: r := runCLI("fix", "--input-kind", "stdin", "file.txt"); assert r.ExitCode == 2

tests.title: A mismatched --input-kind, under any of the four values, is a usage error before anything is fetched, read beyond the check, or a model is resolved
given: for each of file, issue and stdin, an argument that does not match that kind
tests.when: for any (input-kind, mismatching argument) pair drawn from {(file, an issue URL), (issue, a plain string), (stdin, a non-'-' string)}
then: the run exits with code 2
error.category is usage
no model is resolved
tests.pseudocode: for (kind, arg) in mismatches: r := runCLI("fix", "--input-kind", kind, arg); assert r.ExitCode == 2; assert r.Envelope.Error.Category == "usage"

tests.title: impl with --input-kind text on an ordinary spec reference is unaffected by a same-named file existing elsewhere on disk
given: a spec package directory referenced by id "07"
a file named "07" also existing elsewhere on disk
tests.when: impl is run with --input-kind text and the argument "07"
then: codeimpl.Locate resolves the same package directory it resolves without --input-kind
Resolve's ordinary file check never ran
tests.pseudocode: withFlag := runImpl("--input-kind", "text", "07"); without := runImpl("07"); assert withFlag.Result.SpecDir == without.Result.SpecDir

tests.title: --dry-run is registered exactly once, on Common, with the one make-no-remote-change definition
given: Common.Register is called for each of the four tools
tests.when: the resulting flag sets are inspected
then: each tool's flag set has exactly one --dry-run flag, defined by Common
its help text is the same string on every tool
tests.pseudocode: for tool in tools: f := tool.FlagSet.Lookup("dry-run"); assert f != nil; assert f.Usage == commonDryRunUsage

tests.title: Each tool's usage text states the correct local meaning of --dry-run
given: the usage constant in each of cmd/issue, cmd/fix, cmd/spec, cmd/impl's main.go
then: issue's usage says --dry-run does nothing locally
spec's usage says it writes no files either
fix's and impl's usage name the branch and the commits as still happening
tests.pseudocode: assert !mentionsLocalEffect(issueUsage); assert contains(specUsage, "writes no files"); assert contains(fixUsage, "branch") && contains(fixUsage, "commit"); assert contains(implUsage, "branch") && contains(implUsage, "commit")

tests.title: --total-budget is registered exactly once on Common, defaulting to zero (no ceiling)
given: Common.Register is called
then: Common.TotalBudgetUSD is 0
a run with the per-phase --budget set but no --total-budget is not stopped by any total-budget check
tests.pseudocode: c := &Common{}; fs := flag.NewFlagSet(); c.Register(fs); fs.Parse([]); assert c.TotalBudgetUSD == 0

tests.title: issue applies min(--budget, --total-budget) as its one phase's effective ceiling
given: issue invoked with --budget 10 --total-budget 4
issue invoked with --budget 4 --total-budget 10
tests.when: the effective ceiling for the one phase is computed for each
then: the first run's effective ceiling is 4
the second run's effective ceiling is 4
tests.pseudocode: assert effectiveCeiling(budget:10, totalBudget:4) == 4; assert effectiveCeiling(budget:4, totalBudget:10) == 4

tests.title: fix stops with category budget before the implementation phase when cumulative spend already exceeds --total-budget at the analyse/implement boundary
given: a fix run with --total-budget set below what the analyse phase alone already spent
tests.when: the pipeline reaches the boundary between analyse and implement
then: the run stops before the implement phase starts
the envelope's error.category is "budget"
tests.pseudocode: r := runCLI("fix", "--total-budget", "0.01", input); assert r.Envelope.Error.Category == "budget"; assert !r.ImplementPhaseRan

tests.title: spec stops with category budget before a scope's PRD phase when --total-budget is exceeded, and an unsplit input has no interior boundary
given: a spec run on an input that splits into three scopes, with --total-budget set below the cumulative spend before the second scope's PRD phase
a separate spec run on an input that does not split, with the same --total-budget
then: the split run stops with error.category "budget" before the second scope's PRD phase, with its split plan left in place
the unsplit run is bound only by the single-phase min(--budget,--total-budget) fold, like issue
tests.pseudocode: rSplit := runCLI("spec", "--total-budget", "low", splittingInput); assert rSplit.Envelope.Error.Category == "budget"; assert len(rSplit.Result.SplitPlan) > 0; rUnsplit := runCLI("spec", "--total-budget", "low", unsplitInput); assert rUnsplit.EffectiveCeiling == min(budget, totalBudget)

tests.title: A flag one tool does not use, but another tool defines, is rejected naming both the flag and the accepting tool
given: impl invoked with --label, a flag issue defines
then: the run exits with code 2
the error message names "--label" and names "issue" as the tool that accepts it
